subject: Renewal: staggered GPU reservation & throughput addendum
messages:
From: Lucinda Park <lucinda.park@aerodyne.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: procure@aerodyne.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Renewal proposal questions — Aerodyne

Hi Markus,

Thanks for sending the high-level renewal numbers last week. A few follow-ups from procurement and engineering before we route to legal:

- We plan to expand our Dedicated footprint by ~8 additional A100-class GPUs across two reserved pools (low-latency search & batch inference). Can Redwood accommodate a staged activation (i.e., 4 GPUs start on renewal + 4 GPUs 30 days later) and bill pro‑rata?
- For procurement we need explicit throughput guarantees per pool (tokens/sec) and a clear SLO/credit calculation for when we miss targets.
- We'd like a short fallback policy in case of capacity shortage (e.g., automated routing to lighter-weight quantized variants or regional burst). Please include concrete TPS numbers and SLO language we can review.

I've attached our utilization extract and the SOW the procurement team will attach to the PO.

Can you confirm by EOD Monday whether the staged reservation is possible and share draft addendum language?

Best,

Lucinda Park
Head of Platform Ops, Aerodyne Systems
lucinda.park@aerodyne.ai

Attachments: aerodyne-utilization-report-q2-2027.xlsx, aerodyne-procurement-sow.xlsx

From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: Lucinda Park <lucinda.park@aerodyne.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal questions — Aerodyne

Hi Lucinda — thanks for the clear note and the utilization file. Short answers up front: staged activation is supported, and we can propose per-pool throughput guarantees plus a credit formula based on tokens shortfall over a rolling window.

Draft proposal (summary):

- Capacity: +8 GPUs total split into two reserved pools: Pool A (search) = 4 GPUs active at renewal T+0; Pool B (batch) = 4 GPUs active at renewal T+30 days.
- Billing: pro‑rata for the second pool until full billing period; phased invoice schedule to match activation windows.
- Throughput guarantees (per pool):
  - Pool A: 60,000 tokens/sec sustained baseline; 100,000 tokens/sec 5‑minute burst window.
  - Pool B: 40,000 tokens/sec sustained baseline; 80,000 tokens/sec 5‑minute burst window.
- SLO language (proposed):
  - Availability: Redwood guarantees that the reserved pool will supply the sustained throughput for at least 99.5% of minutes in any 30‑day rolling window.
  - Latency SLO (optional add): For 95% of requests routed to Pool A, end-to-end generation P50 < 120ms and P95 < 400ms measured at Redwood ingress under steady load.
- Credits: If sustained throughput falls below the guaranteed sustained baseline for more than 60 aggregated minutes in a 24‑hour rolling window, customer receives service credits computed as 5% of the monthly reserved fee for each 60-minute block below threshold, capped at 50% for the period. Credits apply per pool independently.
- Fallbacks: Automated routing to quantized model variants in the same region for up to a 10% latency increase; cross-region burst allowed if explicitly enabled in config.

I've attached a draft addendum (redwood-staggered-addendum-v1.pdf) that contains the legal-friendly SLO paragraphs and the activation schedule. This is intentionally conservative — we can tighten latency targets or adjust credit percentages if Aerodyne prefers stronger latency SLAs in exchange for a higher committed fee.

Next steps: 1) Quick internal review (we need legal to look at the credit calc), 2) I can push a redline by Thursday, 3) finalize DocuSign link for signatures.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Markus Klein
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-staggered-addendum-v1.pdf

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Aerodyne renewal — pricing/term notes

Markus / Neha — quick internal threading so legal and pricing ops can triage before I send to the customer. Lucinda signaled they want per‑pool credits and phased billing. Key items: 

- Confirm whether credit calc should be per‑pool (Markus suggested yes) — this impacts how we meter aggregated tokens.
- Need a recommended tradeoff table: stronger latency SLOs in exchange for higher committed fee (I propose +12% for P95 latency guarantees).
- Procurement asked for pro‑rata billing on Pool B activation; confirm accounting treatment for month-of-change.
- We should pre-author a one-time onboarding credit to smooth the first billing cycle.

I'll draft the pricing sheet for AE-0421-RNW and loop legal with the addendum.

Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Lucinda Park <lucinda.park@aerodyne.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: procure@aerodyne.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal questions — Aerodyne

Thanks Markus — the staged approach looks workable. A couple of asks from procurement/legal before we proceed to signature: 

1) We need throughput guarantees reported per pool (not just aggregated). Please update the addendum to show per-pool baseline numbers and confirm the credit calculation will be applied per pool.
2) Credit calculation request: make the credit proportional to the tokens/sec shortfall averaged over a 24h rolling window (not just 60‑minute blocks). Example: if Pool A baseline is 60k and observed sustained average for the 24h window is 50k, credit = ((60k-50k)/60k) * daily reserved fee * 0.2 (20% seriousness multiplier). We don't need exact final language but want a mechanism that scales with shortfall.
3) For billing we prefer phased billing and a single consolidated invoice with line items for each pool activation. Can Redwood accommodate consolidated invoicing?

If you can update the draft to reflect per‑pool credits and propose a DocuSign flow (we prefer a single signature from our CFO), we can move this to PO submission next week.

Best,
Lucinda

Lucinda — thanks, appreciate the specificity. We've updated the addendum per your asks and tightened the credit mechanism to be proportional and per pool. Summary of what's changed in redwood-staggered-addendum-v1 (revised):

- Per-pool baseline numbers called out explicitly for Pool A and Pool B.
- Credits: a proportional credit calculation applied per pool using a 24-hour rolling average shortfall formula. Concrete example added in Section 3.2 so procurement can preview math. Credit multiplier reduced to 15% (from prototype 20%) to balance operational risk and avoid outsized credits on transient noise.
- Invoicing: Redwood will issue a consolidated invoice with separate line items per pool activation. Pool B will be billed pro‑rata until its first monthly anniversary then billed at the full monthly reserved fee.
- Activation windows: Pool A goes live at Renewal + 0 days; Pool B at Renewal + 30 days. We will run an automated capacity validation (internal test traffic) 48 hours prior to Pool B activation and confirm with Aerodyne.
- Fallbacks: clarified that cross-region burst must be explicitly enabled by Aerodyne and is billable if used.

Next steps: 1) I'm attaching the revised addendum and the example credit calc worksheet; 2) Marissa, please attach the pricing worksheet we discussed and finalize the consolidated invoice sample; 3) Once Aerodyne signs, we schedule Pool B activation and the validation window.

I've added a DocuSign link here for review: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/ae-0421-rnw-sign

If this looks good Lucinda, I can push to legal for final redline and route the DocuSign envelope for your CFO.

Regards,

Markus Klein
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
